property_details.address: Primary manufacturing site, South East England

observations: The asset base is aging, with total accumulated depreciation representing 60% of gross book value.
The principal manufacturing asset (powder coating line) was a significant investment in FY22-23 at £1.3m cost.
The company operates an asset-light model with a fixed asset intensity of only 4.9% of turnover.
The balance sheet is substantially unencumbered with no material finance leases or asset-backed lending, suggesting high refinancing potential.
Significant intangible assets exist off-balance sheet, including trademarks, pending patents, and proprietary software.
Total staff cost base of £2.86m equates to 15.6% of FY25 turnover.
60% of headcount is in production and cost-of-sales functions.
The leadership team has significant tenure, with the CEO having 15 years of service.
Two overhead functions (People/HR and Marketing) were expanded during FY26 to support forecast growth.

summary_insights: Revenue demonstrated strong recovery in FY25, growing 31.1% following a 9% dip in FY24, indicating robust market demand.
Gross margin improved significantly from 27.4% in FY23 to 37.8% in FY25, driven by the normalisation of raw material prices and internal manufacturing efficiencies.
Net profit margin expanded dramatically from 1.5% to 10.4% over the three-year period, reflecting high operational leverage as the business scaled.
Financial resilience has strengthened considerably, with the interest coverage ratio rising from 3.8x to 40.8x, indicating a very low-risk debt profile.
Operating expenses were well-controlled, increasing only 21% over two years despite a 34% increase in gross profit, contributing to EBITDA margin expansion.
A red flag exists regarding the FY25 audit, which carries a qualified opinion concerning the verification of £2.6m in inventory.
The business has successfully transitioned through a period of heavy investment in FY23 to achieve high profitability and cash generation by FY25.
The balance sheet demonstrates a significant 36.4% growth in net assets in FY25, driven by strong retained profitability.
Liquidity remains robust with a current ratio of 2.78 and a quick ratio of 1.82 in FY25, indicating excellent short-term debt coverage.
The company has aggressively deleveraged, with total liabilities decreasing from £3.6m to £3.35m while the asset base expanded.
Cash reserves have more than doubled over the period, rising from £1.33m in FY23 to £2.92m in FY25.
Net current assets (working capital) expanded by 32% in the final year, strengthening the firm's financial resilience.
Long-term debt has been almost entirely cleared, with the gearing ratio dropping from 19.7% to a negligible 0.17% by FY25.
Fixed assets have steadily depreciated without major new capital expenditure, suggesting a shift toward a more asset-light or cash-generative phase.
